extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners and communicators (PRSA members and nonmembers) seeking to improve PR writing and news-release skills
extracted.subtask_description: A professional development course syllabus describing modules and lesson-level criteria for effective PR writing — with emphasis on news releases, backgrounders, proofreading, and advanced persuasive/storytelling techniques to increase reach and measurable results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach and results as primary goals
rubrics_metrics.description: When it comes to PR writing, what someone 'thinks' about your writing takes a backseat to what they DO (or don’t do) because of your writing. The only thing that matters is reach and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure and measure writing choices by their ability to expand reach and create measurable improvement in results rather than by stylistic preferences alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing like a journalist without being one
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing techniques that position your copy to persuade while remaining unshakably believable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt journalism-influenced clarity and credibility to earn placements, page views and shares — even if you are not a trained journalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why most PR writing is set up to fail (and exploit it)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand common structural and strategic failures in PR writing and use that knowledge to improve persuasion and placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify predictable weaknesses (e.g., jargon, poor leads) and counter them with targeted tactics taught in the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt the 'Excellence-Based' standard for PR writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Move to a new standard of PR writing quality described as 'excellence-based.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use excellence-based benchmarks to judge copy and prioritize changes that increase credibility, clarity and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be direct: pursue simplicity over complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: How to be direct: trading in the complicated for the simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer plain, straightforward phrasing that makes the point quickly; avoid convoluted sentence structures that bury the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplify impact: double or triple the power of your writing
rubrics_metrics.description: How to double or triple the power of everything you write.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific techniques (strong leads, vivid examples, focused calls to action) to increase persuasive force of each sentence and paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove your case responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond a Reasonable Doubt: How to 'Prove Your Case' Without Crossing the Line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with evidence and context while avoiding overstatement or unethical exaggeration; balance persuasion with credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show and tell: bring words to life
rubrics_metrics.description: The Power of Show and Tell: How to Bring Your Words to Life; and Making Them Believe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete examples, anecdotes and sensory detail to make assertions believable and memorable; follow with techniques to strengthen readers' belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove jargon — write accessibly
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Jargon' mistake and how to fix it; Remove Jargon: Write Accessibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate specialized terms or explain them simply so general audiences and journalists can understand and use your copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the evolution of the news release
rubrics_metrics.description: The Evolution of the News Release and How to Use It Today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate release formats and tactics that fit today's media environment (print and online) rather than relying on outdated templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chameleon principle: set the proper tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chameleon Principle: How to Set the Proper Tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone to the audience and context (journalists, management, stakeholders) so your copy reads appropriately to each target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping strategy for news releases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mapping Strategy: How to Write News Releases That EVERYONE Loves; and Getting Past the Gatekeepers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mapping approach to structure releases that satisfy both journalists and organizational management and that anticipate editorial gatekeeping behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomy of a successful news release
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anatomy of a Successful News Release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a functional structure (lead, key facts, quotes, boilerplate, contact info) and ensure each element serves placement and clarity goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead: what to say first
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Off on the Right Foot: What to Say First.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a compelling, journalist-friendly lead that communicates the most newsworthy information immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make quotes work
rubrics_metrics.description: Making Quotes Work: Why Most News Release Quotes Put Readers to Sleep and a Detailed Strategy for Making Yours Effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace clunky, generic quotes with vivid, quotable lines that add perspective, emotion or context and are useful to journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEO-aware writing without robotic copy
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Think Like a Search Engine Without Writing Like a Robot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize headlines and body copy for discoverability (search) while preserving natural, human-readable language and journalistic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write effective backgrounders and op-eds
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Write Backgrounders and Op-Eds That Get Results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor longer-form explanatory pieces to editorial standards and persuasive goals, using narrative, evidence and clear argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness: put writing on a diet
rubrics_metrics.description: Putting Your Writing on a Diet: The Secrets to Saying More by Writing Less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut unnecessary words, sentences and qualifiers to make copy tighter and more forceful; prefer brevity that preserves meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repetition and redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: How Not to Repeat Yourself, Repeat Yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and remove needless repetition that dilutes impact and bores readers; use repetition only when rhetorically deliberate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clichés
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clichés Trap and How It Can Ruin Your Writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of tired phrases that reduce originality and credibility; replace clichés with concrete, specific language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short and sweet: move readers forward
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Use 'Short and Sweet' to Move Readers Forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short sentences and paragraphs strategically to maintain momentum and guide reader attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and avoid credibility-destroying mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Destroy Your Credibility in 100 Words or Less: Horrifying Examples of Bad PR Writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn from bad examples (overclaiming, factual errors, sloppy grammar) to avoid actions that immediately undermine trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Making It Perfect: Tips and Tricks for Proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply systematic proofreading techniques (read aloud, use checklists, multiple passes) to catch errors before distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid embarrassing word mix-ups
rubrics_metrics.description: How To Avoid Word Mix-Ups That Make You Look Dumb (Ouch!).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be vigilant for commonly confused words and homophones; ensure word choice communicates intended meaning precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be your own grammar police — write error-free
rubrics_metrics.description: Becoming Your Own Grammar Police: How to Write Error Free, Part I & II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop habits and reference checks to eliminate grammar mistakes that harm credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write in pictures: apply creativity without distracting
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing in Pictures: Applying Creativity Without Distracting Your Readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid imagery and creative devices sparingly so they enhance rather than distract from the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the element of surprise strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastering the Element of Surprise: How to Use It to Stand Out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce unexpected angles or facts to capture attention while ensuring relevance and appropriateness for the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose words that keep readers engaged
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Choose the Words That Keep Readers Engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select precise, active, engaging language that maintains momentum and avoids passive or dull phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage storytelling interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Leveraging the Never-Ending Interest in Story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate narrative techniques (characters, conflict, stakes) to make factual PR copy more compelling while staying accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a distinctive writing style
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Your Own Writing Style Revolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a consistent, memorable voice that sets your writing apart while remaining appropriate to the brand and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow a repeatable writing process
rubrics_metrics.description: Tying It All Together: The 14-Step Smarter Writing Process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a structured multi-step process for drafting, revising, proofreading and optimizing copy to ensure quality and consistency.
